ALDEx3 fixed- and mixed-effects analysis

Source: R/aldex3.R
step_aldex3.Rd

Fit planned contrasts with the official ALDEx3 engine. Fixed models use native linear regression; mixed models use exact lme4 fits, not the approximate blmm engine. A centralized add_model() is required.

Usage

step_aldex3(
  rec,
  max_significance = 0.05,
  nsample = 2000,
  scale_model = "clr",
  scale_args = list(gamma = 0.5),
  p_adj_method = "BH",
  n_cores = 1,
  seed = 130L,
  rarefy = FALSE,
  id = rand_id("aldex3"),
  engine_args = list()
)

Arguments

rec

An unprepared Recipe object.

max_significance

Native adjusted P value cutoff.

nsample

Number of Monte Carlo draws passed to ALDEx3. Default 2000.

scale_model

One of "clr", "tss", "sample", "coefficient".

scale_args

Named list of scale-model parameters; see Details.

p_adj_method

Native multiple-testing adjustment, default "BH".

n_cores

Number of cores for native mixed-model fitting, default one.

seed

Integer Monte Carlo seed. Restores the caller's RNG state.

rarefy

Whether to rarefy before fitting; default FALSE.

id

Unique step identifier.

engine_args

Named list with an optional fit list. Supports native test ("t.HC3", "t.HC0", "t") for fixed models and streamsize. Validation is left to ALDEx3. The native test setting does not apply to mixed models. Data, model, scale, engine, seed and two-sided inference are managed by dar.

Value

A Recipe with the ALDEx3 step added.

Details

Supply sequence counts for inference. Taxonomic aggregation and common preprocessing precede native Dirichlet sampling. No extra prevalence filter or implicit "other" feature is added. Filtering changes the composition and the features defining CLR scale assumptions. External scale information must describe the retained community; removed counts are not reconstructed. Native numerical parameters and input values are passed to ALDEx3. Engine-specific validation and errors are left to that package. dar checks its configuration and taxon, sample and contrast identities.

Scale models are specified by name, not executable functions. "clr" and "tss" accept scale_args = list(gamma = 0.5), the native default SD on the log2 coefficient scale. gamma = 0 fixes the corresponding scale assumption. "sample" requires named s.mu and s.sd vectors of external log2-scale means and SDs, one per input sample ID. "coefficient" requires named c.mu and c.sd vectors, one per column of the resolved fixed-effects design. This interface supports independent SDs, not covariance matrices or arbitrary scale functions. The default is a modeling choice, not an estimate of scale uncertainty. Coefficient coding and the units of numeric covariates affect these priors; choose scale information appropriate to the study.

Scale uncertainty and priors always refer to the original resolved design, even when a planned contrast requires releveling. Each contrast uses the same seed and scale-model basis. The native model is refitted for each contrast; mixed models can therefore be expensive.

Effects are mean Monte Carlo coefficients on the log2 abundance scale conditional on the specified scale model (aldex3_log2_abundance_coefficient). Sequence counts alone do not measure absolute microbial load. P values and adjusted P values retain ALDEx3's native directional Monte Carlo procedure, including adjustment across taxa separately for each coefficient. They are not BH applied to averaged P values, nor a joint adjustment over all planned contrasts. Missing statistics remain missing. Execution settings and the effective package version are recorded by get_execution().

See also

Other Diff taxa steps: step_aldex2(), step_ancom(), step_corncob(), step_deseq(), step_lefse(), step_linda(), step_maaslin(), step_rademu(), step_wilcox()

Examples

data(metaHIV_phy)
rec <- recipe(metaHIV_phy) |>
  add_model(~ RiskGroup2, targets = "RiskGroup2", tax_level = "Genus") |>
  step_aldex3(scale_model = "clr", scale_args = list(gamma = 0.5))
# Use verified sequence counts for inference; prep() executes the recipe.
